articles.title: Subject matter and objectives
articles.requirement: Establishes rules for the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and the free movement of such data.

articles.title: Material scope
articles.requirement: Applies to processing of personal data wholly or partly by automated means, and to non-automated processing forming part of a filing system.

articles.title: Territorial scope
articles.requirement: Applies to controllers/processors established in the EU, and to processing of EU data subjects' data by non-EU entities offering goods/services or monitoring behaviour.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines personal data, processing, controller, processor, consent, personal data breach, supervisory authority, and other key terms.

articles.title: Principles relating to processing
articles.requirement: Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly, transparently, for specified purposes, minimised, accurate, stored limitedly, and with integrity and confidentiality. Controller must demonstrate compliance (accountability).

articles.title: Lawfulness of processing
articles.requirement: Processing is lawful only with consent, contractual necessity, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest, or legitimate interests. Controller must identify and document the lawful basis.

articles.title: Conditions for consent
articles.requirement: Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous. Controller must demonstrate consent was given. Withdrawal must be as easy as giving consent.

articles.title: Child's consent for information society services
articles.requirement: Processing of a child's data for information society services requires parental consent where the child is below 16 years (Member States may lower to 13).

articles.title: Processing of special categories of data
articles.requirement: Processing of racial, ethnic, political, religious, biometric, health, sex life, or trade union data is prohibited unless a specific exception applies (explicit consent, employment law, vital interests, etc.).

articles.title: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences
articles.requirement: Processing of criminal conviction and offence data only under official authority control or where authorised by Union or Member State law with appropriate safeguards.

articles.title: Processing not requiring identification
articles.requirement: If the controller does not need to identify a data subject, it is not obliged to maintain or acquire additional data solely to comply with the Regulation.

articles.title: Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject
articles.requirement: Controller must provide information in a concise, transparent, intelligible, and easily accessible form using clear and plain language, especially for children.

articles.title: Information where data collected from data subject
articles.requirement: When collecting data directly, controller must provide identity, purposes, legal basis, recipients, transfer intentions, retention period, and rights information at time of collection.

articles.title: Information where data not obtained from data subject
articles.requirement: When data is obtained indirectly, controller must provide the same information as Art.13 plus the source and categories of data within one month or at first communication.

articles.title: Right of access
articles.requirement: Data subjects have the right to obtain confirmation of processing, access to their data, and information about purposes, categories, recipients, retention, rights, and source.

articles.title: Right to rectification
articles.requirement: Data subjects have the right to obtain rectification of inaccurate personal data and completion of incomplete data without undue delay.

articles.title: Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
articles.requirement: Data subjects may request erasure when data is no longer necessary, consent is withdrawn, processing is unlawful, or there is no overriding legitimate ground.

articles.title: Right to restriction of processing
articles.requirement: Data subjects may request restriction of processing when accuracy is contested, processing is unlawful, data is no longer needed by controller but required by subject, or pending objection verification.

articles.title: Notification obligation regarding rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing
articles.requirement: Controller must communicate any rectification, erasure, or restriction to each recipient unless impossible or disproportionate, and inform the data subject of those recipients on request.

articles.title: Right to data portability
articles.requirement: Data subjects have the right to receive their data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and to transmit it to another controller where processing is based on consent or contract and is automated.

articles.title: Right to object
articles.requirement: Data subjects may object to processing based on public interest or legitimate interests. For direct marketing, the right to object is absolute.

articles.title: Automated decision-making and profiling
articles.requirement: Data subjects have the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produce legal or similarly significant effects, unless authorised by law or based on explicit consent.

articles.title: Responsibility of the controller
articles.requirement: Controller must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and demonstrate that processing complies with the Regulation, taking into account nature, scope, context, and risks.

articles.title: Data protection by design and by default
articles.requirement: Controller must implement data protection principles by design (pseudonymisation, minimisation) and by default (only data necessary for each purpose is processed).

articles.title: Joint controllers
articles.requirement: Where two or more controllers jointly determine purposes and means, they must transparently determine their respective responsibilities by arrangement, and make the essence available to data subjects.

articles.title: Representatives of controllers or processors not established in the Union
articles.requirement: Controllers or processors not established in the EU but subject to GDPR must designate a representative in the Union in writing.

articles.title: Processor
articles.requirement: Processing by a processor must be governed by a contract or legal act setting out subject matter, duration, nature, purpose, data types, and controller obligations. Processor must not engage sub-processors without authorisation.

articles.title: Processing under authority of controller or processor
articles.requirement: Processor and any person acting under the authority of controller or processor who has access to personal data must process only on instructions from the controller.

articles.title: Records of processing activities
articles.requirement: Controllers and processors must maintain written records of processing activities including purposes, data categories, recipients, transfers, retention, and security measures.

articles.title: Security of processing
articles.requirement: Controller and processor must implement appropriate technical and organisational security measures including pseudonymisation, encryption, confidentiality, resilience, restoration ability, and regular testing.

articles.title: Notification of breach to supervisory authority
articles.requirement: Controller must notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach without undue delay and within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless unlikely to result in risk to rights and freedoms.

articles.title: Communication of breach to data subject
articles.requirement: Where a breach is likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms, the controller must communicate the breach to affected data subjects without undue delay.

articles.title: Data protection impact assessment
articles.requirement: Where processing is likely to result in high risk (systematic monitoring, large-scale special categories, automated decision-making), the controller must carry out a DPIA before processing.

articles.title: Prior consultation
articles.requirement: Controller must consult the supervisory authority prior to processing where a DPIA indicates that processing would result in high risk in the absence of mitigation measures.

articles.title: Designation of the data protection officer
articles.requirement: Controller and processor must designate a DPO where processing is by a public authority, involves large-scale systematic monitoring, or large-scale processing of special categories.

articles.title: Position of the data protection officer
articles.requirement: DPO must be involved in all data protection matters, provided with resources, must not receive instructions regarding exercise of tasks, and reports directly to highest management level.

articles.title: Tasks of the data protection officer
articles.requirement: DPO must inform and advise, monitor compliance, provide advice on DPIAs, cooperate with the supervisory authority, and act as the contact point.

articles.title: Codes of conduct
articles.requirement: Member States, supervisory authorities, and the Board shall encourage the drawing up of codes of conduct to contribute to proper application of the Regulation.

articles.title: Certification
articles.requirement: Member States and supervisory authorities shall encourage establishment of data protection certification mechanisms, seals, and marks to demonstrate compliance.

articles.title: General principle for transfers
articles.requirement: Any transfer of personal data to a third country or international organisation may only take place if the conditions of Chapter V are complied with.

articles.title: Transfers on basis of adequacy decision
articles.requirement: Transfers may take place where the Commission has decided that the third country ensures an adequate level of protection. Adequacy decisions are periodically reviewed.

articles.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
articles.requirement: In the absence of adequacy, transfers may proceed with appropriate safeguards including standard contractual clauses, binding corporate rules, codes of conduct, or certification mechanisms.

articles.title: Binding corporate rules
articles.requirement: Binding corporate rules must be approved by the competent supervisory authority and must include application of data protection principles, data subject rights, and acceptance of jurisdiction.

articles.title: Derogations for specific situations
articles.requirement: In the absence of adequacy or safeguards, transfers may occur on explicit consent, contractual necessity, important public interest, legal claims, vital interests, or from a public register.

articles.title: Supervisory authority
articles.requirement: Each Member State must establish one or more independent supervisory authorities responsible for monitoring and enforcing the Regulation.

articles.title: Competence of lead supervisory authority
articles.requirement: The supervisory authority of the main establishment of the controller or processor is the lead authority for cross-border processing, cooperating with concerned authorities.

articles.title: Powers of supervisory authorities
articles.requirement: Supervisory authorities have investigative powers (audits, access), corrective powers (warnings, bans, fines), and authorisation and advisory powers.

articles.title: Right to lodge complaint
articles.requirement: Every data subject has the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority if they consider that processing of their personal data infringes the Regulation.

articles.title: Right to compensation
articles.requirement: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of a GDPR infringement has the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor.

articles.title: General conditions for imposing fines
articles.requirement: Administrative fines up to €10M/2% turnover for controller/processor obligation breaches, and up to €20M/4% turnover for principle, rights, or transfer breaches. Fines must be effective, proportionate, and dissuasive.
